title: Outlook for COE Prices and Proposal for Support for Persons and Firms who Rely On Vehicles to Continue Their Trade
what_it_is: Outlook for COE Prices and Proposal for Support for Persons and Firms who Rely On Vehicles to Continue Their Trade

sections.label: COE price rise questions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Transport about COE price rises, speculation, business costs, affected groups, PHC take-up and possible measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) to what extent can the recent surge in prices of Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) be attributed to speculation; and (b) whether LTA will consider implementing measures to curb such speculation by (i) reducing the transfer period for open category COEs to 30 days to ensure only genuine need-based participants engage in the bidding process and (ii) raising the deposit requirement from $10,000 to 50% or more of the COE price to further deter speculative bidding and uphold the integrity of the COE system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the continued rise in the prices of Certificates of Entitlement will impact business costs and those who depend on their vehicles to earn a living; and (b) whether there are any measures that can moderate further increases in prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport with Certificate of Entitlement (COE) prices continuing to rise (a) which segment of the population is expected to be most impacted; and (b) whether the Ministry will consider reviewing and modifying the COE system to better meet the needs of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) in light of the increased supply of Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) in the third quarter of this year, whether there has been a further increase in the COEs used to register Private Hire Cars (PHCs); (b) if so, what proportion of the additional COEs was taken up by PHCs; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider a different policy approach on COE bidding by PHCs vis-à-vis cars used for personal purposes.

sections.label: Vehicle numbers on roads
sections.summary: The passage states there are about one million vehicles on Singapore roads, including more than 650,000 cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And finally, I will explain the steps we have taken to address the concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We currently have about one million vehicles on our roads, including more than 650,000 cars.

sections.label: Road land and emissions
sections.summary: Roads take up about 12% of total land and the land transport system accounts for about 15% of domestic carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Roads currently take up about 12% of our total land and the land transport system accounts for about 15% of Singapore's total domestic carbon emissions.

sections.label: Public transport subsidies
sections.summary: The Government subsidises public transport by more than $2 billion annually, translating to more than $1 in subsidies per journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To keep our buses and trains running, the Government subsidises public transport by more than $2 billion annually; and this translates to more than $1 in subsidies per journey.

sections.label: Rail network investment
sections.summary: The Government is investing more than $60 billion in the rail network this decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: To achieve these improvements, the Government is investing more than $60 billion in the rail network this decade.

sections.label: PHC driver licence holders
sections.summary: As of September 2023, about 53,000 individuals hold a PHC Driver's Vocational Licence to provide ride-hail services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As of September 2023, about 53,000 individuals hold a PHC Driver's Vocational Licence (PDVL), allowing them to provide ride-hail services using a chauffeured PHC.

sections.label: LTA review of P2P providers
sections.summary: LTA has started a review of the industry structure and regulatory framework for P2P providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) has started a review on the industry structure and regulatory framework for P2P providers to ensure that services stay relevant and are able to meet evolving commuter needs.

sections.label: TCOE validity and forfeiture
sections.summary: The TCOE is valid for six months, and if unused to register a vehicle it expires and the $10,000 bid deposit is forfeited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The TCOE is valid for six months, within which it must be used to register a vehicle, otherwise it expires and the bid deposit of $10,000 is forfeited.

sections.label: COE supply increase outlook
sections.summary: Industry players observed COE supply for these categories will increase significantly from the second half of 2024, peaking in 2026 to 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Looking ahead, industry players have correctly observed that the COE supply for these categories will increase significantly from the second half of 2024 before reaching the peak supply years from 2026 to 2027.

sections.label: Cat A and B quota increase
sections.summary: LTA announced Cat A and Cat B quota supply for the fourth quarter of 2023 will both increase by 35% over the third quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Last Friday, LTA announced that the supply for Cat A and Cat B quota for the fourth quarter of 2023 will both increase by 35%, compared to the third quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I should also point out that the 35% increase in supply for both categories is larger than the proportion of bids won by car-leasing companies in the last three quarters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will also ensure that the COE supply in the upcoming quarters will continue to increase in 2024 till the peak supply years in 2026 and 2027.

sections.label: Cat C quota increase
sections.summary: LTA announced the Cat C quota supply for the current quarter will increase a further 65% over the third quarter of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As LTA announced last Friday, the Cat C quota supply for this current quarter will increase a further 65%, compared to the third quarter of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Similar to Cat A and B, I want to assure our businesses and commercial vehicle owners that the quota supply for Cat C will also continue to increase in 2024 and beyond, before reaching a peak in 2026.

sections.label: Cut-and-fill trade-off
sections.summary: On cut-and-fill, he is right that there is a trade-off.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: First, on "cut-and-fill", he is right that there is a trade-off.

sections.label: More cars in near term
sections.summary: In the near term there is a risk of more cars on the roads before cars are deregistered during peak years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: What it means is that, in the near term, we do have the risk of having more cars on the roads in the next few years, before the cars are deregistered during the peak years.

sections.label: COE quota allocation by category
sections.summary: Of 1,614 additional COEs, 863 went to Cat B, 546 to Cat A and 200 to Cat C, with more additional supply to Cat A than Cat B.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the recent announced COE quota increase of 1,614 additional COEs, the Government has allocated 863 to Cat B; 546 to Cat A and 200 to Cat C.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The second supplementary question is: would the Government consider scrapping the Open category altogether, because it tends to be for the bigger cars, and allocate the COEs in that category to Cat A and Cat C?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, I would suggest maybe Mr Leong can add up the two numbers and he would then see very clearly that, since we started this "cut-and-fill" earlier this year, we have been allocating more additional COE supply to Cat A, and less so to Cat B overall.

sections.label: ARF increase for luxury cars
sections.summary: After the ARF for high-end luxury cars was increased, buying of those cars moderated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The second point about high-end cars, after we increased the ARF for the high-end cars, the luxury cars, we have actually seen a moderation in terms of people buying those cars.

sections.label: COE and ERP congestion control
sections.summary: Congestion policies require both the COE system to control car population and ERP to manage usage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Our policies to control congestion require us to do both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, we control the population of the cars through the COE system, but we also have ERP which manages the usage.

sections.label: Review of P2P services
sections.summary: A recently started review aims to look at how the provision of P2P services can be further enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I just want to ask whether the Senior Minister of State can share what are the likely areas will be looked into under this study?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have just started this review not too long ago, but the purpose is to look at how we can further enhance the provision of P2P services.

sections.label: Cat A versus Cat B share
sections.summary: In 2012, 55% of cars were Cat A, falling to less than 50% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Speaker, on Cat A versus Cat B supply, if we look at the car population statistics, beyond any bidding exercise or even in any given year, but if we look at the population level, in 2012, 55% of cars were Cat A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But this has fallen to less than 50% in 2022.

sections.label: Motorcycle taxes lower for lower-income
sections.summary: ARF, road taxes and ERP charges for motorcycles are lower than other vehicle categories because some Singaporeans rely on motorcycles for their livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If Ms Poa had heard my speech correctly earlier, I said that we do recognise that some Singaporeans rely on motorcycles for their livelihoods and there are higher proportions of lower-income individuals among motorcycle owners compared to car owners, and that is why the ARF, road taxes and ERP charges for motorcycles are lower, compared to the other vehicle categories.

sections.label: ARF tiered by vehicle OMV
sections.summary: The ARF is a bigger and more direct tool that differentiates how much is paid based on different OMV of vehicles, and it is tiered and progressive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Actually, the bigger, and perhaps more direct, tool is the ARF where you very clearly differentiate based on different OMV of the vehicles, how much ARF they have to pay, and it is tiered and progressive.

sections.label: Motorcycle supply needs being studied
sections.summary: The total supply of motorcycles in view of changing and evolving user needs is being studied, but not to the extent of treating them like commercial vehicles with a growth rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The second point is that the total number of supply for motorcycles in view of the changing and evolving needs of the users, I think that is something which, as I pointed out in my reply, we are studying – whether they are ways to achieve a better outcome to reflect the intent of, I think what Mr Singh has in mind and what Mr Murali Pillai had raised earlier as well, but perhaps not going to the extent of treating them like commercial vehicles and having a growth rate.

sections.label: Open category COE deregistration flow
sections.summary: A question was asked about whether a deregistered Open category COE returns to Open category or its registered category, but a mechanism flows part of it back to Open category.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: Just now, there was a question I asked which was not answered and that is when Open category COE is deregistered after being used to register for a certain category, when it is deregistered, does that COE go into Open category again or to the category that it was registered for?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But there is a mechanism to then flow part of it back to the Open category, in order for the quota to be re-allocated again.
